network.overall_strategy: The synthesis network interconnects all literature-supported or credible prebiotic routes to proline, each mapped from its geochemical context. The main mechanistic route is the cyanosulfidic photoredox sequence (Patel et al., 2015), with branching points reflecting competition with arginine, and the fate of intermediates. Supplementary, less-resolved but plausible routes (spark discharge, extraterrestrial ices, parent-body aqueous chemistry, hydrothermal ornithine/arginine pyrolysis, and hypothetical metabolism-first cycles from glutamate) are included as individual pathways, with explicit disclaimer where reaction steps lack experimental demonstration. The network also incorporates the critical hydrolysis and chiral amplification steps (the only plausible source of L-proline), and marks contested or speculative steps per the literature.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-catalyzed HCN-acetylene coupling
reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-catalyzed cross-coupling of HCN and acetylene to give acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This step is shown mechanistically in Patel et al. (2015, Nature Chem.), with Cu(I) accelerating the coupling of HCN and acetylene to acrylonitrile. Critiques concern Cu abundance and staged reagent delivery, but the reaction is supported. [Patel et al., 2015]

reactions.name: Aza-Michael addition: acrylonitrile + NH3

conditions.other: No catalyst is required; neutral pH favorable

reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile to give β-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Ammonia reacts with acrylonitrile under aqueous conditions to form β-aminopropionitrile; demonstrated as a precursor of proline. [Patel et al., 2015]

reactions.name: UV/H2S photoreduction to 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: UV irradiation, presence of H2S as photoreductant

reactions.mechanism: Photoreductive cleavage of the nitrile to the aldehyde using H2S and UV light (254 nm).
reactions.reasoning: Photoreduction with H2S/UV is key to cyanosulfidic chemistry. Yields β-aminopropanal, an established intermediate. [Patel et al., 2015, Figure 1]

reactions.name: Cyclization/hydrolysis to β-alanine
reactions.mechanism: Aldehyde hydration and subsequent hydrolysis yields β-alanine from β-aminopropanal.
reactions.reasoning: β-aminopropanal can be hydrated and hydrolyzed to β-alanine; this is plausible and parallels Strecker-like steps, although not shown as a main branch in Patel et al. (2015). [Speculative but mechanistically justified]

reactions.name: Reductive formation of γ-butyrothiolactam
reactions.mechanism: UV/H2S mediated reduction and cyclization yields γ-butyrothiolactam (cyclic thioamide) from β-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Formation of γ-butyrothiolactam is explicitly reported in the proline route as a key intermediate. [Patel et al., 2015, Scheme 2]

reactions.name: Photoreduction/cyclization to proline α-aminonitrile

conditions.other: UV irradiation; staged addition of HCN

reactions.mechanism: Conversion of γ-butyrothiolactam to cyclic imine and subsequent Strecker capture with HCN yields proline α-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Final photoreduction plus HCN addition completes the mechanistic prebiotic proline precursor synthesis, 32% yield over these steps. [Patel et al., 2015]

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline α-aminonitrile to prolinamide
reactions.mechanism: Stepwise aqueous hydrolysis of the α-aminonitrile's nitrile group to amide.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of aminonitrile to amide is a standard Strecker sequence step, but not directly demonstrated for proline aminonitrile; plausible by analogy. [Patel et al., 2015, with caveat of unquantified yield]

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of prolinamide to racemic proline
reactions.mechanism: Final hydrolysis liberates proline from the amide intermediate.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of the amide to proline closes the Strecker sequence. Not directly demonstrated for proline but standard for α-aminonitriles. [Patel et al., 2015 and general Strecker precedents]

reactions.name: Enantiomeric amplification (solid–solution eutectic or phase equilibrium)

conditions.other: Partial solubility with eutectic phase behavior; applies to near-racemic solutions

reactions.mechanism: Seed enantiomeric excess is amplified in solution by selective crystallization with the racemate.
reactions.reasoning: Proline has the best-studied phase-behavior amplification; nearly enantiopure solutions are achievable from a small initial excess (if any), though not in truly prebiotic solvents. [Klussmann et al., 2006, Nature]

reactions.name: Solid-phase hydrolysis of extraterrestrial organic residue
reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of acid-labile residues (from irradiated ices or meteorite organics) releases racemic proline.
reactions.reasoning: Proline detected after hydrolysis of organic residues in UV-irradiated ices (Muñoz Caro et al., 2002; Bernstein et al., 2002) and meteorites (Kvenvolden et al., 1970; Glavin et al., 2025). Mechanism not established but product is unambiguous. [Muñoz Caro et al., 2002; Glavin et al., 2025]

reactions.name: Spark discharge Strecker–like amino acid synthesis

conditions.other: Reducing to neutral atmosphere; mixture of products

reactions.mechanism: Electrical discharge yields complex organic mixture containing HCN and other precursors. Inferred Strecker-type pathway leads to proline.
reactions.reasoning: Proline detected among 20+ amino acids in Miller spark discharge reactions (Ring et al., 1972; Johnson et al., 2008). Mechanistic details for proline not isolated but strongly inferred. [Ring et al., 1972; Parker et al., 2011]

reactions.name: Parent-body aqueous alteration (Strecker/fischer–tropsch)
reactions.mechanism: Strecker/catalytic formation of amino acids in aqueous parent-body settings, possibly followed by hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: Proline detected in Murchison, Bennu, Ryugu, and parent-body hydrolysates. Exact mechanism for proline not established. [Kvenvolden et al., 1970; Glavin et al., 2025; Parker et al., 2023]

reactions.name: Cyanamide guanidinylation (competing arginine branch)
reactions.mechanism: Cyanamide enables guanidinylation of β-aminopropionitrile skeleton, diverting flux toward arginine-type products.
reactions.reasoning: When cyanamide is present, the cyanosulfidic network generates arginine aminonitrile alongside proline's. This is a documented branchpoint in the Patel et al. (2015) route. [Patel et al., 2015]

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of arginine α-aminonitrile to arginine
reactions.mechanism: Stepwise hydrolysis of arginine aminonitrile intermediate to arginine.
reactions.reasoning: Analogous to proline aminonitrile hydrolysis; plausible based on Strecker paradigm but untested for this specific molecule. [Patel et al., 2015]

reactions.name: Reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate to glutamate
reactions.mechanism: Reductive amination over mineral catalysts forms glutamic acid from α-ketoglutarate (not shown but inferred from CO2 fixation).
reactions.reasoning: Reductive amination to glutamate is demonstrated in FeS/Ni(OH)2/hydrothermal systems. Precursor keto acid steps plausible; route stops here for proline as next step (reduction to GSA) is not prebiotically demonstrated. [Huber & Wächtershäuser, 2003; Kitadai et al., 2019]

reactions.name: Reduction of glutamate to glutamate-5-semialdehyde (hypothetical)
reactions.mechanism: Reduction of terminal carboxyl to aldehyde (as GSA).
reactions.reasoning: No prebiotic demonstration exists for this step, but included to model the metabolism-first pathway. Considered a key bottleneck. [Speculative; see Kitadai et al., 2019; Mayer & Moran, 2022]

reactions.name: Cyclization of GSA to P5C
reactions.mechanism: Spontaneous cyclization of glutamate semialdehyde to pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C).
reactions.reasoning: This cyclization is thermodynamically favored and nonenzymatic; established in both biology and prebiotic simulation. [Smith & Greenberg, 1956]

reactions.name: Reduction of P5C to proline (speculative)
reactions.mechanism: Imine reduction to pyrrolidine ring (proline).
reactions.reasoning: No prebiotic reduction demonstrated for P5C to proline, but the step is simple in chemical synthesis and could be mediated by H2/Ni or FeS. [Speculative; see Mayer & Moran, 2022; Biology uses pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase]

reactions.name: Hydrothermal cyclization/pyrolysis: ornithine to proline
reactions.mechanism: Cyclodeamination: α-amino group attacks δ-carbon, closes ring (ornithine to proline).
reactions.reasoning: Formation of proline from ornithine/arginine in hydrothermal pyrolysis detected (Vallentyne, 1968); product assignment is from older analytics and needs re-examination. [Vallentyne, 1968; Körner et al., 2021]

reactions.name: Hydrothermal deamination: arginine to ornithine
reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis and deamination of arginine yields ornithine.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrothermal pyrolysis of arginine was shown to produce ornithine (and proline); included for network completeness. [Vallentyne, 1968]

reactions.name: Hydrothermal rearrangement: glutamate to ornithine
reactions.mechanism: Transamination and rearrangement; not well established, but ornithine can theoretically arise from glutamate under certain hydrothermal conditions.
reactions.reasoning: This is a hypothetical extension included to connect protometabolic and pyrolytic pathways. Not directly demonstrated prebiotically. [Speculative; see biochemistry and prebiotic analogs]

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic photoredox route to proline (Patel et al.)
pathways.description: Surface UV and H2S enable a Cu(I)-catalyzed HCN–acetylene coupling and photoreduction sequence from HCN and acetylene to L-proline (via aminonitrile and hydrolysis).

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic–β-alanine side branch
pathways.description: An alternative pathway through β-alanine formation from β-aminopropanal and subsequent (speculative) ring closure/hydrolysis to proline.

pathways.name: Competing arginine branch (guanidinylation)
pathways.description: Flux diversion via cyanamide to arginine aminonitrile, showing pathway competition at β-aminopropionitrile.

pathways.name: Meteorite/ice delivery and post-hydrolysis release of proline
pathways.description: Proline released by acid hydrolysis of extraterrestrial organic matter (meteorite or UV-processed ice residues).

pathways.name: Spark discharge Strecker chemistry route (inferred)
pathways.description: Electrical discharge creates mixed prebiotic organics, combining HCN, aldehydes, and NH3 to yield racemic proline upon work-up.

pathways.name: Parent-body aqueous alteration (meteorite)
pathways.description: Strecker and catalytic routes on meteoritic parent-bodies yield proline, isolated after hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Metabolism-first: glutamate pathway (speculative beyond Glu)
pathways.description: Hydrothermal synthesis of glutamate from CO2 and NH3, followed by hypothetical reduction to GSA, cyclization to P5C, and reduction to proline.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal ornithine/arginine → proline cyclization (pyrolysis)
pathways.description: Pyrolytic cyclodeamination of ornithine or arginine in hydrothermal fluids yields proline directly.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal rearrangement: glutamate to ornithine to proline
pathways.description: Links protometabolic (glutamate) and pyrolytic (ornithine) proline synthesis branches.

pathways.name: Chiral phase-behavior amplification to L-proline
pathways.description: Seed enantiomeric excess in proline is amplified via solid–liquid equilibrium in the presence of eutectic/phase behavior, giving high L-proline ee.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the mechanistically validated cyanosulfidic photoredox pathway as per Patel et al., including all accepted intermediates and branches. However, the deterministic charge and atom balance check reveals that most steps after the first two are unbalanced (rxn_003, rxn_005, rxn_006, rxn_007 show conservation violations, e.g., persisting N, H, O or S discrepancies). This signals missing or mis-specified small molecules (water, NH3, etc.), which reduces chemical feasibility. Hydrolysis to proline is not confirmed by yield in the literature and is atom-unbalanced as written. The pathway is geochemically and mechanistically sound but should be revised to fix mass/charge balance and to clarify the fate of unaccounted atoms. Environmental context is plausible, but the 'Surface' designation could be clarified (e.g., freshwater evaporite, flow vs. stagnant, UV exposure details).
suggestions: Assign all participating small molecules (e.g., balance for H2, NH3, H2O, etc.) in reactions rxn_003, rxn_005, rxn_006, rxn_007, rxn_008
Refine product/reactant formulas and check for tautomeric ambiguities
Clarify any tacitly involved oxidants/reductants and solvent details per the literature
State explicitly that hydrolysis yields for aminonitrile → proline are unreported

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway describes a plausible cyanosulfidic branch to β-alanine (via 3-aminopropanal and β-aminopropionitrile), but suffers from the same balance issues as P1 for the photoreduction and hydrolysis steps. The steps are chemically reasonable as per the Patel et al. mechanism. Hydrolysis from prolinamide to proline remains problematic and unbalanced. Pathway coherence is good, but the terminal relevance to proline biosynthesis is lower.
suggestions: Re-balance the photoreduction and hydrolysis reactions and specify missing byproducts.
Clarify the fate of β-alanine in the context of proline synthesis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This 'arginine branch' is chemically plausible up to the arginine aminonitrile, with guanidinylation supported by the literature. However, hydrolysis steps (rxn_014, 020 and 019) are unbalanced and lack experimental evidence for hydrothermal, nonenzymatic Arg/Orn→Pro conversion. The pathway correctly reflects cyanamide as a competing branch; however, steps after arginine lack validation and violate mass/charge balance.
suggestions: Clarify all byproducts and attempt to balance hydrolysis/cyclization reactions.
Explicitly label steps beyond arginine as speculative in a nonenzymatic context.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway reflects the detected presence of proline in extraterrestrial residue after hydrolysis, not a demonstrated abiotic route. Both steps are atom/charge unbalanced and mechanistically ill-defined: rxn_010 in particular does not conserve C/H/N, and proline must be released from unknown precursors rather than formed directly. This is a valid 'detection route,' but not a mechanistic synthesis.
suggestions: Express these as detection events, not as synthetic steps.
Clarify the unknown nature of the precursor(s) and avoid implying mechanistic detail where none exists.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This spark discharge Strecker pathway reflects the literature detection of proline in Miller-type experiments. However, the steps are grossly unbalanced as written (rxn_011: not all C/H/N accounted for) and lack characterized intermediates specific to proline (e.g., pyrroline intermediates are only inferred). This aligns with literature as a detection route but does not constitute a valid stepwise synthesis.
suggestions: Clearly designate these as detection-only where intermediate mechanisms are undemonstrated.
Supply speculative, balanced intermediates if possible or refrain from mechanistic detail.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This parent-body aqueous alteration route is literature accurate as a detection pathway, but the actual steps (rxn_012, rxn_008) are highly unbalanced and not mechanistically justified for proline. The route is included correctly as a detection outcome, but should not imply stepwise synthesis where none exists.
suggestions: Present this as a detection outcome, not a resolved pathway.
Clarify that the chemistries operating on parent bodies lack proline-specific mechanistic data.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This speculative 'metabolism-first' pathway is correctly marked as hypothetical in the literature. Reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate to glutamate is shown experimentally under hydrothermal/mild aqueous conditions; however, all subsequent steps to proline (reduction and cyclization of GSA/P5C, reduction to proline) have not been demonstrated abiotically. Atom-balance is poor in all but the first step. The pathway's inclusion is valid for completeness but does not represent a feasible synthetic route at present.
suggestions: Explicitly label the Glu→Pro portion as speculative and undemonstrated.
Attempt to achieve atom balance if further mechanistic proposals are made.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The hydrothermal ornithine/arginine → proline branch correctly models literature indications of Arg/Orn conversion to proline under pyrolytic/hydrothermal conditions, but as per Körner et al. 2021 and Vallentyne 1968, the product identity is not secure and experimental demonstration is lacking. Both steps are unbalanced. This is a speculative/degradation pathway, valid for inclusion but not viable as a robust synthetic path.
suggestions: Label as speculative and attempt to balance N loss/transfer for completeness.
Add citations detailing the uncertainty of this pathway.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway forms a plausible concatenation of hypothetical glutamate → ornithine → proline in hydrothermal contexts. However, neither side-chain extension (rxn_021) nor cyclization/deamination (rxn_019) is demonstrated prebiotically, and both steps are unbalanced. Overall, inclusion is useful for metabolic completeness but remains highly speculative.
suggestions: State explicitly the absence of prebiotic demonstration for the key steps.
Attempt balanced equations or suggest possible byproducts/side reactions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The chiral amplification (phase equilibrium/eutectic enrichment) of proline is very well-supported in the literature (Klussmann et al. 2006; Blackmond 2021). The reaction is physically valid and environmentally appropriate as written, provided some racemic or slightly enantioenriched proline is available. The caveat is that natural environments likely offer lower amplification than CHCl3/cosolvate systems. This step does not itself create proline, but it robustly achieves L-proline enrichment from racemic starting material.
suggestions: Specify solvent/system (aqueous, ternary solution, etc.) for prebiotic relevance.
Reference the literature limits of amplification in the absence of cosolvents.

evaluation.network_feedback: This network comprehensively and accurately encodes all plausible and literature-supported routes to proline, including speculated and detection-based branches, and is clear on environmental and mechanistic context. The explicit mapping of chiral amplification is commendable. Major weaknesses arise from gross atom and charge conservation violations in 17 of 21 reactions (including all critical cyanosulfidic and hydrolysis steps), principally due to unspecified byproducts and/or errors in product/reactant formulas. While these can often be remedied with explicit small-molecule additions, their current omission lowers the chemical feasibility and overall scientific reliability of the network. All speculative/hypothetical pathways are correctly flagged, and convective/atmospheric/environmental assignments are consistent with literature. Target achievement is robust, reaching L-proline through multiple plausible intermediates. To reach the 'excellent' threshold: (1) fix all mass and charge imbalances, (2) clarify speculative designations for undemonstrated steps, and (3) improve chemical detail for detection-based branches. As it stands, the network is good and holistic, but not yet excellent or fully valid until the conservation violations are resolved.
